authors: Paoul S. Martinez, Caryn E. Plummer
title: Ophthalmology of Crocodilia: Alligators, Crocodiles, Caimans, and Gharials
why: Textbook chapter on the crocodilian eye: pupil, fundus, tapetum and visual streak in alligators and caimans, which would give the alligator rows their own source.

authors: April R. Beatty, Mark Flint, Jaylene B. Flint, Anne J. Gemensky‐Metzler, Dubraska V. Diaz-Campos, Joany C. van Balen et al.
title: ASSESSMENT OF OPHTHALMIC DIAGNOSTIC PARAMETERS, CONJUNCTIVAL FLORA, AND PHARMACOLOGIC DILATION OF A LARGE POPULATION OF JUVENILE AMERICAN ALLIGATORS (ALLIGATOR MISSISSIPPIENSIS)
journal: Journal of Zoo and Wildlife Medicine
why: Pupil diameter and dilation in 165 juvenile American alligators, the only large measured sample of Alligator mississippiensis eyes.

authors: André Tavares Somma, Leandro Lima, Rogério Ribas Lange, Amália Turner Giannico, Fabiano Montiani‐Ferreira
title: The eye of the red‐eared slider turtle: morphologic observations and reference values for selected ophthalmic diagnostic tests
why: Eye anatomy and reference values of the red-eared slider, the most photographed turtle in Alachua County ponds.

authors: Helga Kolb, J. H. Jones
title: Light and electron microscopy of the photoreceptors in the retina of the red‐eared slider, Pseudemys scripta elegans
why: Photoreceptor types of the red-eared slider retina, to confirm the number of cone classes.

authors: Christa Neumeyer, Jutta Jäger
title: Spectral sensitivity of the freshwater turtle Pseudemys script a elegans: Evidence for the filter-effect of colored oil droplets
why: Spectral sensitivity of the red-eared slider and the filter effect of its coloured oil droplets.

authors: Karen M. Davis, Gordon M. Burghardt
title: Turtles (Pseudemys nelsoni) learn about visual cues indicating food from experienced turtles.
why: Behavioural test of what Florida redbelly turtles (Pseudemys nelsoni) learn from visual cues, a species of its own in north Florida.

authors: Karen M. Davis, Gordon M. Burghardt
title: Long-term retention of visual tasks by two species of emydid turtles, Pseudemys nelsoni and Trachemys scripta.
why: Visual discrimination retained by Pseudemys nelsoni and Trachemys scripta over months.

authors: Paul A. Liebman, Gerald Entine
title: Visual pigments of frog and tadpole (Rana pipiens)
why: Visual pigments of Rana pipiens as adult and tadpole, for the leopard frog's own pigment values.

authors: James K. Bowmaker, Ellis R. Loew
title: The action of hydroxylamine on visual pigments in the intact retina of the frog (Rana temporaria)
why: Rana temporaria visual pigment measurements by hydroxylamine bleaching, for the common European frog.

authors: A.-C. Aho, Kristian Donner, S. Helenius, Lis Olesen Larsen, Tom Reuter
title: Visual performance of the toad (Bufo bufo) at low light levels: retinal ganglion cell responses and prey-catching accuracy
why: Low-light prey catching and ganglion cell responses in the common toad Bufo bufo, the European toad.

authors: Cervino NG, Elias-Costa AJ, Pereyra MO, Faivovich J.
title: A closer look at pupil diversity and evolution in frogs and toads.
why: Survey of pupil shape across frogs and toads including North American treefrogs and bullfrogs, to settle the horizontal pupil assumption.

authors: Nadia G. Cervino, Agustín J. Elias‐Costa, Patricia P. Iglesias, Carola A. M. Yovanovich, Julián Faivovich
title: Insights into the evolution of photoreceptor oil droplets in frogs and toads

why: Oil droplets in frog and toad photoreceptors, across many species.

authors: Carola A. M. Yovanovich, Taran Grant, Almut Kelber
title: Differences in ocular media transmittance in classical frog and toad model species and its impact on visual sensitivity
why: Ocular media transmittance in Rana, Bufo and other model frogs, which sets the ultraviolet cut-off.

authors: Zhang B, Wei P, Cui Y, Zhang Y, Chen H, Li X et al.
title: Recurrent evolution of ultraviolet vision in frogs and toads is linked to transitions in locomotor mode.
why: Ultraviolet vision recurring in frogs and toads and tied to locomotor mode, possibly covering treefrogs.

authors: Ute Mathis, Frank Schaeffel, Howard C. Howland
title: Visual optics in toads (Bufo americanus)
why: Visual optics of the American toad Bufo (Anaxyrus) americanus, focus and refraction.

authors: Yanding Zhang, Charles Straznicky
title: The morphology and distribution of photoreceptors in the retina of Bufo marinus
why: Photoreceptor types and distribution in the cane toad retina.

authors: Igor I. Pushchin
title: Retinal ganglion cell distribution and spatial resolution in the Asiatic toad Bufo gargarizans (Günther, 1859)
why: Ganglion cell map and acuity in the Asiatic toad, a measured Bufo for the spatial resolution row.

authors: Linda M. Nowak, Daniel G. Green
title: Flicker fusion characteristics of rod photoreceptors in the toad
why: Flicker fusion of toad rods (Bufo marinus), to check the cane toad flicker figure against its source.

authors: Frederic P. Gaillard, H. Roussel
title: The Visual Field of a North-African toad Bufo mauritanicus
why: Visual field of a North African toad Bufo mauritanicus, to extend the field of view figure.

authors: Arnold J. Sillman, P�l R�hlich, Jeffrey Allen Southard, Ellis R. Loew, VICTOR I. GOVARDOVSKII
title: The photoreceptors and visual pigments of the garter snake ( Thamnophis sirtalis ): a microspectrophotometric, scanning electron microscopic and immunocytochemical study
why: Photoreceptors and visual pigments of the common garter snake, measured by microspectrophotometry; the best-measured snake that is also widely photographed.

authors: Rachel Wong
title: Morphology and distribution of neurons in the retina of the american garter snake Thamnophis sirtalis
why: Retinal ganglion cell types and their spread across the garter snake retina, to give the snake sharp-vision area.

authors: Leo J. Fleishman, Ellis R. Loew, Martin J. Whiting
title: High sensitivity to short wavelengths in a lizard and implications for understanding the evolution of visual systems in lizards

why: High sensitivity to short wavelengths in a lizard; check which lizard and whether it bears on Anolis or Sceloporus.

authors: Guillem Pérez i de Lanuza, Enrique Font
title: Ultraviolet vision in lacertid lizards: evidence from retinal structure, eye transmittance, SWS1 visual pigment genes, and behaviour
why: Ultraviolet vision in lacertid lizards (SWS1 pigment, eye transmittance), a European genus the reptile view also covers.

authors: Mélissa Martin, Jean‐François Le Galliard, Sandrine Meylan, Ellis R. Loew
title: The importance of short and near infrared wavelength sensitivity for visual discrimination in two species of lacertid lizards
why: Short-wavelength and near-infrared sensitivity in two lizard species, to see whether the reptile view's violet tint holds for common lizards.

authors: Ellis R. Loew
title: A third, ultraviolet-sensitive, visual pigment in the Tokay gecko (Gekko gekko)
why: Third, ultraviolet-sensitive pigment in the Tokay gecko, to widen the gecko pigment count beyond Hemidactylus turcicus.

authors: Lina S. V. Roth, Linda Lundström, Almut Kelber, Ronald H. H. Kröger, Peter Unsbo
title: The pupils and optical systems of gecko eyes
why: Pupils and optical systems of gecko eyes, with the multifocal rings that bear on a slit pupil's blur.

authors: Birgit Weyand, Meir Israelowitz, Matthias Reuter, Sabine Bohlmann, Robert A. Wagner, Syed W. H. Rizvi et al.
title: Morphological Study of the Infrared Sensory Pits of Pit Viper, Python and Boa Snakes
why: Morphology of the infrared pits of pit vipers, pythons and boas, for where the pit looks relative to the eye.

authors: Leonard Kass, Michael S. Loop, Peter H. Hartline
title: Anatomical and physiological localization of visual and infrared cell layers in tectum of pit vipers
why: Where visual and infrared inputs meet in the pit viper tectum, for how the two pictures are combined.

authors: Allison C. Alberts
title: Ultraviolet visual sensitivity in desert iguanas: implications for pheromone detection
why: Ultraviolet sensitivity measured in desert iguanas, a relative of the green iguana.

authors: Frank Schaeffel, Alan de Queiroz
title: Alternative Mechanisms of Enhanced Underwater Vision in the Garter Snakes Thamnophis melanogaster and T. couchii
why: Underwater vision of two garter snakes, to check the garter snake's focus in water.
